key: O mankind! Be careful of your duty to your Lord Who created you from a single soul and from it created its mate and from them twain hath spread abroad a multitude of men and women.
s: Opening a chapter of laws on orphans, inheritance, marriage and lewdness, the verse addresses all people; al-Tabari, on 4:1, reads it as teaching that all are children of one father and mother, owing each other a brother’s right, the strong giving the weak their due.

evidence.words: ومنبِّهَهم بذلك على أن جميعهم بنو رجل واحد وأم واحدة= وأن بعضهم من بعض، وأن حق بعضهم على بعض واجبٌ وجوبَ حق الأخ على أخيه، لاجتماعهم في النسب إلى أب واحد وأم واحدة= وأن الذي يلزمهم من رعاية بعضهم حق بعض، وإن بَعُدَ التلاقي في النسب إلى الأب الجامع بينهم، مثل الذي يلزمهم من ذلك في النسب الأدنى= وعاطفًا بذلك بعضهم على بعض، ليتناصفوا ولا يتظالموا، وليبذُل القوي من نفسه للضعيف حقه بالمعروف
evidence.gloss: (He describes Himself as sole Creator of all from one person,) alerting them thereby that all of them are the children of one man and one mother, that they are of one another, that the right of each upon the other is binding as a brother’s right upon his brother, since they meet in descent from one father and one mother; that what binds them to regard one another’s right, however distant the common ancestor, is like what binds them in nearer kinship; and so turning them in kindness to one another, that they deal fairly and do not wrong each other, and that the strong render to the weak his due in kindness.

reason: Key verse verbatim (verse.js ok, An-Nisa 4:1, at 493). Plain sense faithful: 4:1 opens the day’s passage, which runs to orphans (4:2 to 4:10), inheritance (4:11 to 4:14), lewdness (4:15 to 4:16) and marriage (4:19 to 4:25), and the ayah addresses mankind; no four-word run from the verse. In the packet on 4:1 al-Tabari, in his own voice before the reports, says God alerts all people that they are children of one man and one mother, that each owes the other a brother’s right, and that the strong must give the weak his due: the sentence carries exactly this. I read his whole comment on 4:1 (and the Ibn Kathir, al-Qurtubi and Jalalayn sections): no contrary preference by al-Tabari. Evidence is one contiguous span (proposer’s ellipsis replaced by the full text); 45 words; entry-check ok.
